comment: Do not take professor Williams. SHE IS NOT AN EASY GRADER. I am not sure if she changed her grading system but after recently taking her class she is a very tough grader. I would meet with her for office hours all the time then she would tell me a correction on my work & proceed to take points off FOR THE CORRECTION SHE VERBATIM TOLD ME TO MAKE.

She is very nice, but not helpful in the class if you are wanting to learn. Lab reports are easily graded, but she is unhelpful and hard to contact for help on assignments. Professor would lecture at the beginning of each lab for about 45 minutes, then through the 3 hours correct what she taught us. Relied on the lab assistant to answer questions.
She is very understanding and a very nice professor.

This lab is the easiest thing ever. She does go on a 30-minute rant at the beginning of class, but the lab itself is so easy to do well in. The grading system is stupid, you get an E, G+, G, but she grades nicely and basically gives you the correct answers everytime. I would take her lab again because its an easy A.

Everyone on here seems to hate on Dr. Williams. She's definitely not great, however, if you're stuck taking a lab with her it's not the end of the world. Pre-lab lectures are lengthy and all over the place so I would probably avoid taking her as a primary lecturer. She is accessible outside of class for office hours and one on one she is helpful.

The other reviews sum it up nicely. 

TLDR: She doesn't know the lab protocols well enough to answer questions.

Dr. Williams is a genuinely sweet person and tries to help if she can. Keyword, IF. A lot of the time, Dr. Williams has absolutely no idea what is going on ever... she made us read a buret wrong on the very first day. Our saving grace in that class was our TA. Her Chem141Lab isn't terrible but if there are other options, definitely try those.

Please do not take biochemistry lab with this professor. This course was so frustrating because of how unprepared she was. When we had questions, she told us to read the protocol instead of actually helping, never seeming to know what she was doing. By the time our final projects were due, only 2/7 lab reports had been graded and returned to us.

Avoid at all costs. Dr. Williams is a caring person, but is an unorganized and unprepared professor. She constantly gets corrected by students, seems to be just as lost as students during experiments/while using instruments, takes a long time to give any graded lab reports back, and takes off points for small details. This class needs a TA.

If you like wasting your 3 hour lab time and listening to pre-lab lectures that seem like they were the made the night before, then you should definitely take Dr. Williams' class. She constantly gets corrected by students and has to double check her slides after making a point.

There came a point very early on in taking this class where, similar to Odell Beckham Jr. after a career-low 23 yards in 3 passes, I was not having fun anymore. The lectures were disjointed and very confusing, and the professor was regularly unable to answer students' questions during class. Absolutely delay CHEM 326 to a later semester.
Do you know when in Impractical Jokers they give the guys a presentation to read that they haven't ever seen before? This is like lectures with Dr. Williams.

This class was a mess. Williams literally will teach something incorrectly then realize it ten minutes later and have to spend 20 minutes going back and fixing what was wrong. I only did decently because I took chem 1 and 2 in high school and do not recommend her to anyone until she makes some significant changes to her teaching. READ REVIEWS

Tests consisted only of a couple questions, if you miss one or two, you fail. She often did not know the answers to her own questions/ problems and was corrected by students consistently. Relies 100% on the lectures which are dense and can be hard to follow, she seems to be very unclear about what she is teaching at times. Save yourself, don't take

Visibly confused with most of the topics that came on the PowerPoint. Is always behind the lab class by 2 weeks, only reads off the powerpoints, is always late posting assignments and grading tests. Often corrected by students. Only take this class if you already have a strong understanding of chemistry.

Professor is often confused by her own content and lectures, and is very reliant on powerpoint presentations. Does not explain concepts well at all, and often gets her own example problems wrong and is corrected by students. DO NOT take her class. I only managed a passing grade due to the help of a chemistry- inclined friend.

she constantly gets her own problems wrong and has no idea what she teachers. extremely behind in content and she does not teach for the weekly online quizzes. if you get her, DROP ASAP. you will learn nothing and will hate chemistry because of this class.

Have not been taught a single thing all of 1st semester, exams are graded in a manner where lots of points are docked off for small details that should be worth 0.5 pts. Will redo the same problem on the board 100 times, going over her explanation in circles until a student corrects her about it. Dont. take. this. class.
does NOT teach anything. drop the course if you do end up in the class.

This teacher does not know how to teach. Her lectures consist of reading class material straight off the board with the expectation that it will pass as teaching. At times it seems like she is unsure off the concepts, often corrected by the students themselves. You are better off learning chem on your own!

We covered a lot of the same material that was covered in Biology 200. I did not find the lectures to be super engaging and the material could have been presented in a clearer format. I think I may have gotten more out of the class if there was a lab component.
Do not. Whatever you do. Do not take this course.
